FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Nutrition Sectional Committee had been approved -by the Food and Agriculture Division Council.
Halwa or

Seera is a sweet dish of Indian culinary popularly consumed all over India. It is traditionally prepared by roasting wheat semolina in fat/oil and adding to it suitable edible oil or fat, sugar ayd water and cooking it till it gelatinises to form a thick gel, but retaining its partial granular structure.

quantity of The proces of making Halwa, from the ready mix, involves adding appropriate water to the mix and mild heating. Due to the ease in cooking and the convenience it provides, the ready mix is gradually gaining popularity. This product also has potential for use in Defence for pack rations and in various expeditions. Ready Suji-Hah+,a mix is prepared by roasting the wheat semolina, cooking and drying various ingredients and subsequently dry-mixing various ingredients so as to provide a homogenized mixture having a characteristic flavour of roasted semolina and light amber-brown colour. favours may be used as Roasted dry fruits like cashewnuts, almonds, raisins and permitted optional ingredients. Some ready mixes contain large amounts of fats. To ensure that these do not get rancid during storage, the committee considered it necessary to lay down the maximum limit of alcoholic acidity of extracted fat. At persent data on this characteristics is not available. However investigations on this part are currently being carried out in various laboratories, and on availability of data, an amendment incorporating this limit will be issued to the standard.

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard READY SUJHL4LWA MIX - SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements methods of sampling and test for ready Halwa mix. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed in Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, ready SujiHalwa mix shall mean a mix containing roasted wheat semolina, edible fats or oils ( see 4.1.2) and sugar with or without ingredients given in 4.2 and prepared by cooking and drying various ingredients and subsequently mixing these so as to provide a homogenized mixture having a characteristic roasted flavour and light amber-brown colour. 4 INGREDIENTS 4.1 Essential Ingredients The ready Suji-Halwa mix shall be made the following essential ingredients. from to and Suji5 REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Description 5.1.1 The ready Suji-Halwa mix shall be of light amber-brown colour, free from any charred or burnt particles. It shall have a light roasted arama and shall be free from any gritty taste. It shall be free from any unpleasant rancid, musty, tallowy or any other stored odour or flavour and any insects or fungus infestation or microbial deterioration. It shall also be free from any added colours and artificial sweetners. Permitted flavours may, however, be added. 5.1.2 When the ready Halwa mix is boiled with water for 5 minutes, it shall attain the characteristic gel structure of freshly prepared Halwa free from cooked lumps or any other textural defects. 5.1.3 When tested by the method prescribed in Annex B of IS 13264 : 1991 the material shall be free from dirt and other extraneous matter. 5.2 Microscopic Examination When subjected to microscopic examination, the material shall not reveal any foreign material other than those specified in 4. 5.3 The material under packed IS 2491 : 1972 ). shall be manufactured conditions hygienic and ( see

Standard Mark

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau qf fndian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by Details of conditions under RI'S for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau.o:f Indian Standards.
